capabilities.capability: Downloadable example projects that go with the lessons, so each tool can be tried on real material.
capabilities.pro_use: Studios hand these to new hires and freelancers so they can learn the house tools on known scenes.

match.note: Doodleberry's demo films each exercise a feature set and double as golden-frame fixtures; no lesson text goes with them.

capabilities.capability: Video walkthroughs for the more complex tools (camera, puppet layer).
capabilities.pro_use: Teams use them to onboard artists quickly, without a trainer.

match.note: Teaching mode (turn a pipeline into a step-by-step tutorial) is in WP-28's scope.

capabilities.capability: A manual in several interface languages (French, Japanese, Chinese planned).
capabilities.pro_use: International studios and outsourcing partners work from the same reference.

match.note: Doodleberry is in-house with one owner and agents; its docs are English. Localising film content is a separate matter (film.localize, WP-25).

chapters.chapter: Download, install and manage your license

capabilities.capability: Installers for Windows, macOS and Linux, with per-OS setup steps.
capabilities.pro_use: IT teams roll the same version out across a studio's mixed workstations.

match.note: engine.doctor lists what the machine has and lacks with the exact fix; tools/setup.sh applies them idempotently.

capabilities.capability: Licence activation, rehosting and troubleshooting through a copy-protection system (software or dongle).
capabilities.pro_use: Studios move seats between machines and recover after hardware changes.

match.note: Doodleberry is in-house and built on open-source parts; there are no seat licences. Third-party licence classes are tracked separately (licence.ledger).

capabilities.capability: Network installation for many seats from one server.
capabilities.pro_use: Large studios deploy and update all workstations centrally.

match.note: One machine runs every command over CLI, HTTP and MCP; render workers on several machines, sharing a content-hash cache, come in WP-38.

capabilities.capability: A modular interface where every panel can be detached from the main window and arranged across several monitors.
capabilities.pro_use: Animators keep the canvas on the tablet display and timeline, colour and light table on a second screen.

match.note: Studio is a set of separate browser pages (timeline, review, board, Rig Canvas) that can sit on different screens, but the layout cannot be saved. A combined, arrangeable desk belongs with WP-21.

capabilities.capability: Rooms: saved workspaces for each stage of the work (storyboard, roughs, clean-up, compositing).
capabilities.pro_use: Artists switch their whole layout when they move from roughing to cleaning or compositing.

match.note: The nearest equivalent for agents is a command subset per role (director, animator, editor), in WP-21.

capabilities.capability: A timeline that carries layer drawings, camera keys, effect keys, notes and audio tracks in one view.
capabilities.pro_use: Everything that is timed in a scene can be checked against everything else at a glance.

match.note: The Studio timeline has shot, dialogue (with word ticks) and clip lanes. A camera-keys lane is in WP-19 and audio waveform lanes in WP-40.

capabilities.capability: A layer stack for creating, ordering, grouping, merging, splitting and renaming layers.
capabilities.pro_use: Compositing order and per-layer edits are managed by hand on every scene.

ref: puppet: part order and z controls
match.note: Layering is declarative: set, then underlays, cast in order, then overlays; inside a puppet, part order plus z controls. There is no free stack of drawn layers until drawn levels (WP-35).

capabilities.capability: A playback bar with play, loop, frame step and playback-rate options.
capabilities.pro_use: Animators review timing constantly while drawing.

match.note: The player page (every frame a pure function of time) and the exported web player both play, scrub and step frames.

capabilities.capability: An info bar that reads out cursor coordinates, the colour under the cursor and preview status.
capabilities.pro_use: Artists use it to place elements precisely and check colour values.

match.note: Agents read exact positions from the baked animation (tools/bake.mjs, the PROBE used by review.fix) rather than from a cursor.

capabilities.capability: A new project set up with resolution, frame rate, pixel aspect, field order and background.
capabilities.pro_use: Each production fixes its delivery format before any drawing starts.

match.note: film.create makes the folder; shots.json holds size and fps (1080x1920 at 30 fps is the QA bar). Pixel aspect and fields have no use in a progressive digital pipeline.

capabilities.capability: Loading existing projects, with a list of recent ones.
capabilities.pro_use: Artists hop between scenes all day.

match.note: film.get returns a film's sources and build outputs; prod.status lists the films on the board.

capabilities.capability: Saving and save-as, so successive versions can be kept.
capabilities.pro_use: Teams keep numbered versions to roll back after bad changes.

match.note: film.write validates each source file on write; films are text, so git holds every version.

capabilities.capability: Guidance and features for keeping work safe: backups, local storage, not touching files while they are open.
capabilities.pro_use: Studios guard against lost days of drawing after a crash.

match.note: Films are small text files under version control. Each production session gets its own worktree and branch.

capabilities.capability: Project templates: blank projects with preset resolution, rate and layers.
capabilities.pro_use: Series productions start every episode from the same technical setup.

match.note: Format templates build a storyboard from a brief, with the frame size and pacing rules set. These are narrative templates as well as technical ones.

capabilities.capability: Modify project: resize or resample, crop and change the frame rate of an existing project.
capabilities.pro_use: Re-purposing a scene for a new delivery format or a higher-resolution master.

match.note: film.render with an aspect re-stages a film natively for 16:9 or 1:1, and vector art scales freely. One command for every aspect is in WP-24; higher frame-rate and 4K masters are in WP-37.

capabilities.capability: Rotate, pan and zoom the view without changing the drawing, and open several windows on one project.
capabilities.pro_use: Animators turn the page to draw natural arcs and zoom in for clean-up.

match.note: The Rig Canvas has no view rotation or zoom; drawing-tool upgrades are in WP-18.

capabilities.capability: A canvas background (colour or checkerboard) kept out of exports, with layers stacked on it like cels.
capabilities.pro_use: Artists judge line and colour against neutral or transparent grounds and export with alpha.

match.note: Synfig and Grease Pencil render characters with alpha before compositing, and export.lottie can leave out the set (background none). Alpha video deliverables are in WP-23.

capabilities.capability: Display overlays: stencil, paper texture, current selection, an animator disc and a safe frame.
capabilities.pro_use: Artists see framing and masking aids while drawing.

match.note: Safe areas are measured by qa.run and drawn as overlays on brand assets. Live drawing overlays belong in the Rig Canvas tools (WP-18).

capabilities.capability: A set of natural-media raster brushes (pen, pencil, airbrush, crayon, oil, watercolour-like) with many settings.
capabilities.pro_use: Frame-by-frame animators draw roughs, clean lines and painted backgrounds in the one program.

match.note: The Rig Canvas has one pressure ink (perfect-freehand), and puppet.from_ink keeps a real pen's texture from a scan. Textured brush engines (Krita, libmypaint) come through WP-34 and WP-18.

capabilities.capability: Pen gestures (pressure, tilt, speed, direction) mapped to brush parameters through editable curves.
capabilities.pro_use: Line weight that responds to the hand is central to the look of hand-drawn animation.

match.note: Pressure (or a speed-simulated pressure with a mouse) drives ink width in the Rig Canvas. Mapping to other parameters, and tilt, is in WP-18.

capabilities.capability: Custom brushes cut from any drawing, with stamp spacing and wet profiles, plus animated brushes that cycle through several images.
capabilities.pro_use: Studios build a brush kit for a show's signature texture; animated brushes stamp foliage or crowds fast.

match.note: Painting and brush engines are WP-34 candidates; scatter of animated stamps also touches WP-42.

capabilities.capability: Drawing modes that decide how a stroke combines with what is already there: colour, behind, erase, shade, light, colorize, panto and others.
capabilities.pro_use: Painting behind line art and shading without masks speeds up clean-up and colour.

match.note: The Rig Canvas bucket tucks fills under the ink, which acts like a 'behind' mode. Layer-level blend modes are in WP-36.

capabilities.capability: Shape tools: freehand strokes, lines, rectangles, ellipses and circles (2 and 3 point), and Bezier or B-spline curves, filled or outlined.
capabilities.pro_use: Used for props, layouts and clean geometric elements.

match.note: Vector paths are native puppet and kit data, and puppet.import flattens basic SVG shapes. Interactive shape tools in the Rig Canvas are in WP-18.

capabilities.capability: Papers: grain textures applied through the brush, including two papers at once.
capabilities.pro_use: Gives digital drawings the tooth of real paper, a signature of the medium.

match.note: The paper set and the post presets (paper, grain) texture the whole frame. Medium simulation for each stroke (pencil, marker, crayon) is in WP-15.

capabilities.capability: Line smoothing (stabiliser), either in real time or after the stroke.
capabilities.pro_use: Clean-up artists get steady, confident lines without redrawing.

match.note: Strokes are simplified after drawing (Ramer-Douglas-Peucker); a live stabiliser is in WP-18.

capabilities.capability: Cut, select and crop tools: rectangle, freehand and colour-based selection, a selection brush, and cropping.
capabilities.pro_use: Artists isolate parts of a drawing to move, fix or reuse them.

match.note: Polygon cuts split a drawing into rig parts (with overlap seams). General lasso and selection editing are in WP-18.

capabilities.capability: A colour panel with A/B colours, sliders, a picker, a mixer, palettes, a colour wheel, variations and a history.
capabilities.pro_use: Colourists keep a show palette and mix related shades fast.

match.note: Colours are named palette slots in puppets and a measured brand palette (brand.check). There is no interactive mixer, which agents do not need.

capabilities.capability: Construction guides with snapping: grid, field chart, circles, ellipses, angle lines, segments, vanishing points and image guides.
capabilities.pro_use: Layout artists draw in correct perspective; animators keep arcs and paths true.

match.note: No drawing guides yet; they fit the Rig Canvas tools of WP-18.

capabilities.capability: A safe-area guide showing title-safe and action-safe zones.
capabilities.pro_use: Keeps important action and text clear of cropping on delivery.

match.note: qa.run measures every word's box against the platform-safe area of each aspect; brand.assets draws safe-area QA overlays.

capabilities.capability: Tool presets and a tool history to recall configured brushes.
capabilities.pro_use: Artists switch between rough, clean and colour brushes many times an hour.

match.note: Belongs with brush engines (WP-34) and the Rig Canvas tools (WP-18).

capabilities.capability: Panning a drawing or selection across the canvas, on one image or across many.
capabilities.pro_use: Repositions drawings during clean-up or fixes registration between frames.

match.note: Characters are moved by keyed placement (x, y, scale). Moving drawn pixels needs drawn levels (WP-35).

capabilities.capability: Transform: scale, rotate, shift and flip with handles or typed values, a movable pivot, applied to one frame or many.
capabilities.pro_use: Adjusts the size and staging of drawings without redrawing.

match.note: Scale, flip and move are placement data, and rotation comes through part angles about pivots. A whole character's rotation is not a placement field.

capabilities.capability: Perspective: four corner points distort a drawing.
capabilities.pro_use: Fits a drawing onto a receding surface such as a sign or a floor.

match.note: Corner-pin distortion fits the per-shot compositor.

capabilities.capability: Warp: an elastic grid with pins that bends pixels smoothly.
capabilities.pro_use: Fixes proportions or adds organic bends to a finished drawing.

ref: puppet: mesh strokes with skinning (v0.5), bendy limbs
match.note: Bone-driven mesh deformation exists in the puppet format (SVG renderer). Free pin warping of a drawing fits WP-35 drawn levels, or the compositor (WP-36).

capabilities.capability: Transformation resampling that preserves image quality, with a preview-quality option.
capabilities.pro_use: Avoids softening line art when drawings are scaled or rotated repeatedly.

match.note: Vector art is resolution independent, but raster parts are resampled by the browser with no quality control. 4K masters are in WP-37.

capabilities.capability: Animation layers: each layer is a strip of drawings, like a roll of film shown on the canvas.
capabilities.pro_use: The core of frame-by-frame work: every character, effect and background is drawn layer by layer.

match.note: Drawn levels (a sequence of drawings with exposures) are the new part type of WP-35.

capabilities.capability: Instances and exposure cells: one drawing held for any number of frames, and instances split or joined.
capabilities.pro_use: Timing on ones, twos or threes, and holds, are set per drawing.

match.note: style.step animates a shot or character on 12s, 8s or 6s. Exposure per drawing comes with WP-35.

capabilities.capability: Adding or removing exposures and instances, shrinking a layer, and reversing a run of images.
capabilities.pro_use: Retiming hand-drawn animation without redrawing.

match.note: timeline.edit retimes and resizes clips, but not drawings.

capabilities.capability: A layer's start frame and moving a whole layer in time.
capabilities.pro_use: Offsets overlapping actions and syncs an element to sound.

match.note: move_clip moves a clip layer, and times can be line-relative so they follow the dialogue after re-voicing.

capabilities.capability: Moving, cutting, copying and pasting images within a layer and between layers.
capabilities.pro_use: Reuses drawings and rearranges keys while blocking.

match.note: Needs drawn levels.

capabilities.capability: Navigation from instance to instance and selection of instance ranges.
capabilities.pro_use: Animators flip quickly between keys while in-betweening.

match.note: timeline.get gives every clip's resolved start and end, and the Studio nudges by frame. Key-to-key navigation and a keys lane are in WP-19.

capabilities.capability: Layer folders that group layers and move them together.
capabilities.pro_use: Keeps big scenes with many characters and effects tidy.

match.note: A character is a group of parts with one timeline, and a shot groups its cast. Arbitrary user folders arrive with drawn levels (WP-35).

capabilities.capability: Flipping a layer horizontally or vertically.
capabilities.pro_use: Reverses a character's facing or reuses a drawing mirrored.

match.note: flip is 1 or -1 per cast member.

capabilities.capability: Pre and post behaviour: what a layer shows before its first image and after its last (nothing, hold, loop, ping-pong), now also per folder.
capabilities.pro_use: Cycles (walks, flames, idles) run for a whole scene from a few drawings.

ref: shots.json: timeline clips (looping base layers such as idle)
match.note: Clips can loop and base layers fill the gaps between gestures. Ping-pong and pre/post settings for drawn levels are in WP-35.

capabilities.capability: Per-layer opacity, and layer attenuation during playback.
capabilities.pro_use: Dims reference layers and builds transparent effects.

match.note: Opacity and mattes for each layer belong to the compositor.

capabilities.capability: Locking layers against accidental edits, and collapsing them to save room.
capabilities.pro_use: Protects approved backgrounds or clean lines while others are worked on.

match.note: WP-39 adds assignments and locks on films and characters.

capabilities.capability: A background preview proxy that caches played frames, with settings for quality and memory.
capabilities.pro_use: Smooth real-time playback of heavy scenes on ordinary machines.

match.note: The live player renders frames on demand, the animatic takes seconds, and renders are cached per shot by content hash so only changed shots re-render.

capabilities.capability: Colour groups: tag layers with colours to show, hide, select or protect them together.
capabilities.pro_use: Organises dense scenes by character or department.

match.note: Timeline organisation features fit the timeline room upgrade (WP-19).

capabilities.capability: Layer blending modes (multiply, screen, add, overlay and so on) and merging layers through a mode.
capabilities.pro_use: Shadows, glows and colour tints are composited from separate layers.

match.note: Blend modes are in WP-36's node compositor scope.

capabilities.capability: Bookmarks and coloured image marks that set key drawings apart from breakdowns.
capabilities.pro_use: Lead animators mark keys and breakdowns so assistants know what to in-between.

match.note: review.add pins notes to frames. Marking drawings by role (key, breakdown, in-between) comes with WP-35.

capabilities.capability: Preserve alpha (paint only on existing pixels) and stencils (mask one layer by another's opaque pixels).
capabilities.pro_use: Shading, texturing and recolouring inside line art without leaking.

match.note: Toon shading clips each shape to itself to paint cel shadows. General masks and mattes are in WP-36.

capabilities.capability: Layer presets that set the defaults (type, colour, opacity, mode) of new layers.
capabilities.pro_use: Departments start every scene with a consistent layer setup.

match.note: Only meaningful once drawn layers exist (WP-35); style defaults today live in dbe/profiles.json.

capabilities.capability: A light table (onion skin) showing nearby frames faded and tinted, with per-frame opacity and modes by instance, frame, bookmark, rig key or image mark.
capabilities.pro_use: Essential for in-betweening and checking spacing in hand-drawn animation.

match.note: The Rig Canvas 'Onion' only shows the rest of the character faintly (a spatial guide, not frames in time). Onion skins over time are in WP-35.

capabilities.capability: Out of pegs: slide the onion-skin frames on top of each other, without changing the drawings, to line them up for in-betweening.
capabilities.pro_use: Animators line up overlapping volumes when an in-between travels a long way.

match.note: Part of the onion-skin work in WP-35.

capabilities.capability: Flipping: roll through a few drawings back and forth as one would with paper.
capabilities.pro_use: The quickest check of a motion's flow while drawing.

match.note: film.preview scrubs a film, but flipping drawings belongs to WP-35.

capabilities.capability: Sketch panel presets for roughing in colour and cleaning up in a separate pass.
capabilities.pro_use: The usual rough, tie-down and clean-up workflow.

match.note: Clean-up of rough lines is in WP-35's scope.

capabilities.capability: An animator panel of one-click actions such as setting a layer to ones, twos or threes or adding exposure.
capabilities.pro_use: Speeds up retiming and layer housekeeping.

match.note: Stepped timing per shot or character exists; per-drawing exposure actions are in WP-35.

capabilities.capability: Repeat images: exposures reuse content from earlier instances to build cycles without duplicating drawings.
capabilities.pro_use: Makes cycles and repeated actions cheap to change.

match.note: Motion clips loop; drawn cycles come with drawn levels.

capabilities.capability: Animated strokes: a single stroke spread over successive frames.
capabilities.pro_use: Fast hand-made effects such as rain, flying insects or sparkles.

match.note: Procedural rain and sparks are in WP-42; hand-made strokes through time fit WP-35.

capabilities.capability: A drawing recorder that replays how a drawing was built, stroke by stroke, as an animation.
capabilities.pro_use: Draw-on reveals for titles, explainers and process videos.

match.note: The kit 'draw' element makes paths draw themselves over time. Recording a live drawing session in the Rig Canvas would join WP-18.

capabilities.capability: An image library per project storing images, sounds, rigs and poses for reuse.
capabilities.pro_use: Shared assets stay consistent across scenes and artists.

match.note: The cast library registers puppets with licence and provenance, and poses and clips travel with each puppet. Props, outfits and set packs are in WP-16.

capabilities.capability: Building a puppet from parts drawn on separate layers grouped in a puppet folder.
capabilities.pro_use: Cut-out characters for TV series where full redraws are too costly.

match.note: Layered SVG, PSD or ORA files become a puppet by layer name, with pivots estimated where markers are missing.

capabilities.capability: Rig mode: placing and editing bones and joints on the drawing.
capabilities.pro_use: Riggers set where each limb bends before animation starts.

match.note: Rigs follow templates (humanoid, doodle), with pivots and cuts that can be confirmed or dragged. Free-form bone layouts and new templates (quadruped, bird, object) are in WP-16.

capabilities.capability: Animate mode: keying bone rotations and positions, with in-betweens made automatically.
capabilities.pro_use: Fast keyed motion for simple actions without drawing in-betweens.

match.note: Rig Canvas posing records keys and saves them as a clip (puppet v0.7). Clips are placed and retimed on the timeline.

capabilities.capability: Squash and stretch of individual members, scaled in both directions.
capabilities.pro_use: Adds elasticity and impact to cut-out motion.

match.note: Per-part squash and stretch (timeline scales, controls, stretchy IK), local to the part so children keep their proportions; every renderer draws it.

capabilities.capability: Bone locking and bone constraints.
capabilities.pro_use: Keeps feet planted and limbs bound while other bones move.

match.note: Two-bone and FABRIK IK with IK/FK blending and targets on other characters, stretchy limbs, foot pins along paths, joint limits, look-at, copy rotation and parent switching exist.

capabilities.capability: Speed curves on rig keys for easing.
capabilities.pro_use: Gives keyed motion weight and accents.

match.note: Keys ease with a fixed smoothstep. Editable curves per key are in WP-19's graph editor.

capabilities.capability: Swapping a member's drawing (mouth, hand, eye shape) at any key from stored poses.
capabilities.pro_use: Lip-sync and hand poses on cut-out characters.

match.note: Swap sets with keyed swaps and controls; visemes come from the voice automatically (voice.build).

capabilities.capability: A pose selector with previews, and adding new poses from existing ones.
capabilities.pro_use: Animators pick from a library of approved poses instead of re-posing.

match.note: Saved poses live in the puppet (used by poses keys in any timeline); the model sheet shows poses and expressions.

capabilities.capability: Saving and importing whole rigs and rigged animations through the library.
capabilities.pro_use: Rigs and stock motions are reused across episodes and artists.

match.note: Clips are template-level, so any character on a template plays any library clip.

capabilities.capability: Turning puppet layers into ordinary frame-by-frame layers for redrawing.
capabilities.pro_use: Animators rough with the rig, then plus the animation by hand.

match.note: The bake (tools/bake.mjs) gives every frame's pose, but there is no conversion into drawn levels to redraw. puppet.export_layers exports only the rest pose.

capabilities.capability: Loading several audio tracks from files or from the library, project-wide or per clip.
capabilities.pro_use: Dialogue, music and effects tracks drive timing in animatics and animation.

match.note: Voices are synthesised and aligned, the score is procedural and foley is automatic. Importing recorded human takes into slots is in WP-13.

capabilities.capability: Per-track settings: mute, volume, colour group, compact or full view.
capabilities.pro_use: Editors balance temp tracks while timing.

match.note: The mix follows rules (ducking, effects below music, panning by screen position). Controls for each track in Studio are in WP-40.

capabilities.capability: Waveform display with drag-to-offset, trimming and a master track summing all tracks.
capabilities.pro_use: Animators read accents and syllables from the waveform.

match.note: Dialogue lanes show lines with word ticks. Waveform lanes and cue trimming are in WP-40.

capabilities.capability: Audio scrubbing: a short piece of sound plays as the playhead is dragged.
capabilities.pro_use: Finds the exact frame of a sound accent.

match.note: Word timings are exact in data (timing.json), but there is no audio scrub in Studio.

capabilities.capability: A stopwatch for tapping beats to measure the rhythm of music or action.
capabilities.pro_use: Timing action to music or to an acted reference.

match.note: The beat grid comes from the score's bpm, and shot changes and line starts are measured against it.

capabilities.capability: Timeline notes: drawn and typed annotations placed along time.
capabilities.pro_use: Directors leave timing notes for animators on the scene itself.

match.note: Notes are pinned to frames, and review.fix turns many of them into data edits.

capabilities.capability: Sound files stored in the project library and dropped on the timeline (12.1).
capabilities.pro_use: Reusable effect and music libraries per show.

match.note: Effect cues are typed (shots.json cues) and come from a synthesised set in the manifest. A sample library (Kenney CC0) is in WP-13.

capabilities.capability: A paint bucket with source options (this layer, another layer, all layers), tolerance, gap closing and antialiasing control.
capabilities.pro_use: Ink and paint: colour fills read the line layer while painting on a separate colour layer.

match.note: The Rig Canvas bucket closes gaps up to about 10 px and tucks fills under the ink, on one drawing. Filling across frames is in WP-35.

capabilities.capability: Fill inside: a brush stroke that only paints inside the closed area it starts in.
capabilities.pro_use: Quick shadow and highlight passes without masks.

match.note: Colour work on drawn frames is in WP-35.

capabilities.capability: Gradient fills (linear, radial, conical, multi-point).
capabilities.pro_use: Soft lighting on characters and props.

match.note: Gradients in imported SVG are flattened, and sets drawn in code use gradients. Gradient fill tools are in WP-18.

capabilities.capability: Opacity mapping to control transparency across a fill.
capabilities.pro_use: Fades and soft-edged fills.

match.note: Mattes and transparency ramps fit the compositor.

capabilities.capability: A colour checker that finds pixels left unfilled next to lines.
capabilities.pro_use: Ink-and-paint QA before shots go to compositing.

match.note: puppet.lint flags raw colours that are not palette slots, and vector fills sit under the ink so they leave no gaps. A per-frame fill check belongs with drawn levels (WP-35).

capabilities.capability: CTG layers: colour a whole animation from a few squiggles, with the colour following the lines as they change from frame to frame.
capabilities.pro_use: Cuts colouring time for frame-by-frame animation by a large factor.

match.note: 'Colour styles applied across every frame' is in WP-35's scope.

capabilities.capability: A CTG palette for editing and extracting colours, so a colour can be changed everywhere at once.
capabilities.pro_use: Colour-model changes (a night version, a corrected skin tone) are applied across a scene.

match.note: Named palette slots recolour a character everywhere, and set_opts recolours sets. Palette variants per scene (night, sick, cold) are in WP-16.

capabilities.capability: CTG textures that stay on coloured areas as they move and change shape.
capabilities.pro_use: Textured looks (fabric, paper, brushwork) on animated characters without boiling by accident.

match.note: Boil and paper grain exist (style.boil, post paper). Textures that track drawn regions fit WP-35, or WP-15 for medium simulation.

capabilities.capability: A key-based 2D camera layer with position, rotation, zoom and size keys on the timeline.
capabilities.pro_use: Pans, trucks and tilts that frame the action, designed in layout.

match.note: Camera keys cover pan and zoom only, and the bake folds them in for every renderer. Camera rotation is missing (it should join WP-19 with the camera-keys lane, or WP-36). There is no camera lane in Studio yet.

capabilities.capability: Camera parameters: format presets, aspect, pixel aspect, fields.
capabilities.pro_use: Matches the camera to the delivery format.

match.note: The frame size is film data, and other aspects are native re-stagings, not crops.

capabilities.capability: Speed curves for ease-in and ease-out of position, zoom and rotation.
capabilities.pro_use: Camera moves that start and stop softly feel filmed rather than mechanical.

match.note: Keys ease with a fixed smoothstep, and auto-framing has an ease setting. Editable curves are in WP-19.

capabilities.capability: Path modes between camera keys: linear, spline or Bezier, with linear sections where needed.
capabilities.pro_use: Curved camera travel around a layout.

match.note: Interpolation between keys is fixed; curve control comes with the graph editor (WP-19).

capabilities.capability: Keyframe management: create, delete, move, copy, invert keys and jump between them.
capabilities.pro_use: Layout artists refine camera timing against the animation.

match.note: Keys are edited as data and may be line-relative. A camera-keys lane is in WP-19.

capabilities.capability: Copying the last camera position of the previous clip to begin the next one.
capabilities.pro_use: Continuity between shots that start where the last one ended.

match.note: Continuity checks and tools are in WP-19.

capabilities.capability: Typed camera moves (12.1) matching common Japanese camera work, recorded on keys and exported with the timesheet.
capabilities.pro_use: The camera intent travels to the compositing studio with the exposure sheet.

match.note: Auto-framing gives a grammar (follow the speaker, wide shots between, punch-ins, handheld). Typed move annotations in interchange formats would join WP-22.

capabilities.capability: An exposure-sheet panel in Japanese or Western layout, one column per layer.
capabilities.pro_use: The standard way to plan and hand off timing between key animators, in-betweeners and compositors.

match.note: The X-sheet is in WP-35, built on OpenToonz's model where WP-34 chooses it.

capabilities.capability: A memo panel, dialogue notes, waveform and camera columns on the sheet.
capabilities.pro_use: Directors and animators plan acting against the dialogue frame by frame.

match.note: timeline.get gives lines with word timings, and the storyboard PDF carries lines and directions per shot. A sheet layout is in WP-35.

capabilities.capability: A dialogue breakdown per frame for lip-sync.
capabilities.pro_use: Animators read mouth shapes from the sheet.

match.note: Visemes come from the voice's phoneme timings automatically, and lipsync.check measures their lag against the audio.

capabilities.capability: Frame roles (key, breakdown, in-between, special in-between) with to-do and done status.
capabilities.pro_use: Tracks who still has to draw what in a scene.

match.note: Key poses with in-between assistance (WP-43) are part of WP-35.

capabilities.capability: Automatic reuse: a new key that shares a name with an existing key takes its content.
capabilities.pro_use: Repeated keys (a return to a pose) stay identical.

match.note: Named poses already exist for rigs (puppet.save); for drawings this needs WP-35.

capabilities.capability: Timesheet export to PDF, and XDTS import and export for exchange with other animation software.
capabilities.pro_use: Sheets go to partner studios and other tools in a shared format.

match.note: The storyboard contact PDF exists (film.storyboard). XDTS fits the X-sheet work in WP-35, and interchange formats are in WP-22.

capabilities.capability: A project organised as scenes and clips (shots), shown as thumbnails, in columns or on a timeline.
capabilities.pro_use: Storyboard artists structure the episode before animation.

match.note: shots.json is the shot list; film.storyboard draws the strip of every shot with its notes.

capabilities.capability: Creating, splitting, joining, duplicating and reordering scenes and clips.
capabilities.pro_use: Restructures the edit as the story changes.

match.note: Shots are edited as data (validated); dragging shots in Studio is in WP-19.

capabilities.capability: Action, dialogue and notes text fields per clip.
capabilities.pro_use: Boards carry the instructions animators need.

match.note: The script lines and directions are data, and the contact sheet prints them beside each shot.

capabilities.capability: Turning the board into an animatic by setting clip durations, with sound and camera moves.
capabilities.pro_use: Directors judge pacing before committing to animation.

match.note: film.animatic holds stills over the mix or voice in seconds (no camera moves); an SVG draft render gives a moving animatic with the camera.

capabilities.capability: PDF publishing of the storyboard with layout options.
capabilities.pro_use: Printed boards for meetings and clients.

match.note: Writes contact.pdf (shots per page with notes) and strip.png.

capabilities.capability: HTML publishing: a web page whose thumbnails play their animation and camera move on hover.
capabilities.pro_use: Shares boards with remote reviewers without software.

match.note: export.web makes a self-contained interactive player of the film; a board page that plays each shot on hover would join WP-19 (review on a phone).

capabilities.capability: EDL publishing: each clip exported as a video, plus an edit list that an editing program can rebuild.
capabilities.pro_use: Hands the animatic to editorial.

match.note: film.cuts writes OTIO per cut; FCPXML and EDL are in WP-22.

capabilities.capability: A bridge between clips (12.1): faint views of the previous clip's last frame and the next clip's first.
capabilities.pro_use: Checks continuity across cuts while drawing.

match.note: qa.run measures seam smoothness at cuts; visual continuity checks (screen direction, eyeline) are in WP-19.

capabilities.capability: Importing images, image sequences and video into layers, either embedded or linked to the source file.
capabilities.pro_use: Brings in layouts, backgrounds, live-action reference and rotoscoping plates.

match.note: Layered drawings and photos become puppets, and video is read for pose by actout.clip. Image or video plates as shot layers fit the compositor (WP-36).

capabilities.capability: Exporting movies and image sequences in many formats (MP4, MOV, AVI, GIF, PNG, TGA, TIFF, PSD), with palette reduction and dithering options.
capabilities.pro_use: Delivers to clients, compositors and the web.

match.note: H.264 MP4 per platform profile. WebM and ProRes with alpha, GIF, APNG and dithered line-art GIFs are in WP-23.

capabilities.capability: A slate burned into exported frames (project name, frame counter, time).
capabilities.pro_use: Review copies are identifiable frame by frame in dailies.

match.note: Burn-ins for review copies fit the review room upgrade.

capabilities.capability: Layered structure export: PSD with layers, CSV with images, the older project format.
capabilities.pro_use: Hands a scene to compositing with every layer separated.

match.note: A puppet exports as a layered SVG, ORA or PSD to repaint. Per-shot multi-pass output (beauty, line, shadow, mattes in EXR) is in WP-37.

capabilities.capability: JSON export that rebuilds the project, with its layers and timing, in a compositing program.
capabilities.pro_use: Moves animation into After Effects for compositing without flattening.

match.note: Lottie and Synfig exports keep parts and keys editable; editor hand-off formats are in WP-22.

capabilities.capability: A sprite-sheet generator.
capabilities.pro_use: Delivers animation to game engines.

match.note: Game runtime export (sprite sheets, Godot) is in WP-30.

capabilities.capability: Cleaning up scanned drawings: removing paper white and grey, cleaning rough pencil lines.
capabilities.pro_use: Paper animators scan their work and prepare it for colour.

match.note: Flattens lighting, thresholds the ink to alpha and removes specks, keeping the artist's line.

capabilities.capability: Peg-hole registration that realigns scans using the peg holes.
capabilities.pro_use: Feeder-scanned drawings play back without jitter.

match.note: Imported paper animation would come in as drawn levels (WP-35).

capabilities.capability: Printing images or sequences with page layouts.
capabilities.pro_use: Paper copies for review or for animating over.

match.note: Storyboard PDFs exist; print-ready stills are in WP-23.

capabilities.capability: Share manager: sending projects, clips or panels to colleagues on the same network.
capabilities.pro_use: Quick hand-offs inside a studio.

match.note: Films move through git branches and worktrees per production session, and characters through the cast library. People and roles are in WP-39.

capabilities.capability: A stand-alone converter that batch-exports projects to many formats without opening the main program, with a client-server mode.
capabilities.pro_use: Render wranglers convert whole episodes overnight.

match.note: Every render runs headless from the CLI or HTTP API; distributed workers are in WP-38.

capabilities.capability: Video input: capturing frames from a camera for stop motion or line tests.
capabilities.pro_use: Animators test paper animation and shoot stop motion directly.

match.note: The camera feeds Act it out (pose to clips) and a photo feeds a doodle puppet. Capturing paper drawings as frames needs WP-35.

capabilities.capability: Clipboard exchange of the current brush or image with other applications.
capabilities.pro_use: Quick round trips to a paint program or chat.

match.note: Agents exchange files and JSON through the CLI, HTTP and MCP rather than a desktop clipboard.

capabilities.capability: A spare image held in memory as a source for certain drawing modes.
capabilities.pro_use: Clones or blends content from a stored image while painting.

match.note: Depends on a brush engine with source modes (WP-34).

capabilities.capability: Swapping the current image with the spare to compare two states.
capabilities.pro_use: Before-and-after checks during clean-up.

match.note: A visual diff between two versions of a film is in WP-19.

capabilities.capability: User-built panels holding buttons for brushes, tools, scripts and menu actions.
capabilities.pro_use: Each studio or artist builds a toolbar for its own pipeline.

match.note: Every command is a tool for agents (CLI, HTTP, MCP, Studio). Curated subsets per role are in WP-21.

capabilities.capability: Action buttons that chain many internal actions as one macro.
capabilities.pro_use: Repetitive pipeline steps become one click.

match.note: Composite commands (film.render, film.heal, film.revoice) already chain steps, and agents script any sequence. Saved user macros and natural-language routing are in WP-21.

capabilities.capability: Exporting a panel with its brushes, scripts and plug-ins as one package file to share.
capabilities.pro_use: Studios distribute their tool kits to every artist and partner.

match.note: Creator packages (rig, boil-preset and loop-pack templates) are in WP-29.

capabilities.capability: A non-destructive stack of effects on a layer, applied in order.
capabilities.pro_use: In-program compositing of glows, blurs and colour without leaving the program.

match.note: Shot-level post (grade, vignette, grain, LUT), motion effects (fx), toon shading and boil are data on a shot. An ordered stack per layer is in WP-36.

capabilities.capability: Preview modes and real-time preview of effects, including on all layers (12.1).
capabilities.pro_use: Artists tune effects while watching playback.

match.note: fx, boil and toon show in the live player; post grades apply only at render (ffmpeg).

capabilities.capability: Stacking, reordering, swapping, renaming and collapsing (baking) effects.
capabilities.pro_use: Builds complex looks step by step and bakes them for performance.

match.note: Node graph editing is in WP-36, with the graph view of WP-20 as its editor.

capabilities.capability: Saving, resetting and reusing effect settings as presets.
capabilities.pro_use: Consistent looks across a show.

ref: shots.json: post presets (crisp, film, warm, cool, paper, noir)
match.note: Named presets plus explicit parameters; the brand kit fixes colours.

capabilities.capability: Keyframed effect parameters, several per effect, interpolated over time.
capabilities.pro_use: Animated glows, fades and colour shifts.

match.note: Post parameters are fixed for each shot today; motion effects are derived from motion, not keyed.

capabilities.capability: Speed curves for effect keys.
capabilities.pro_use: Eases effect animation like any other motion.

match.note: Needs keyed effects (WP-36) and the curve editor (WP-19).

capabilities.capability: Blurs: Gaussian, radial, directional, median, chroma, and motion blur.
capabilities.pro_use: Depth, speed and softening in compositing.

match.note: post.grade accepts ffmpeg filters on the whole frame. Per-layer blurs and depth of field are in WP-36, and sub-frame motion blur in WP-15.

capabilities.capability: Colour correction: curves, histogram, adjustment sliders, tint and colour replacement, black-and-white, multi-colour replace.
capabilities.pro_use: Matches shots and sets mood.

match.note: Post presets, grade filters and a LUT file apply to the whole frame. Colour management (OCIO, ACES) is in WP-37, and per-layer correction in WP-36.

capabilities.capability: Scan clean-up effects: dust cleaner, black-and-white and colour scan cleaners, colour eraser, line colorize.
capabilities.pro_use: Prepares scanned paper animation and recolours line art.

match.note: Ink thresholding and speck removal are in puppet.from_ink. Recolouring the lines of drawn frames is in WP-35.

capabilities.capability: Distortions: bump and displacement maps, warp grid, four-point perspective, kaleidoscope, tornado and wave, optical flow.
capabilities.pro_use: Heat haze, water, impact wobbles and retiming.

match.note: Boil uses cycled displacement fields and flow-based in-betweening proposes drawings (level.inbetween); other distortions are in WP-36.

capabilities.capability: Keying: chroma, luma, colour and cross keyers, plus alpha control.
capabilities.pro_use: Pulls mattes from footage or from colour-coded drawings.

match.note: Mattes are in the compositor's scope; Doodleberry rarely uses live footage.

capabilities.capability: Motion effects: path tools and a path recorder, a pixel tracker, a shaker, stabilisation.
capabilities.pro_use: Attaches elements to moving footage, shakes the camera on impacts, steadies scans.

match.note: Handheld drift, keyed placement and paths for characters and props exist; tracking footage is WP-36.

capabilities.capability: Rendering generators: lighting, volumetric light, lens flare, Perlin noise and plasma, patterns, backgrounds, simple and multi-line text, timecode.
capabilities.pro_use: Generated elements for backgrounds, titles and lighting.

match.note: Text and title elements, sets drawn in code, and toon rims exist. Volumetric light, flares and glows are in WP-36; a timecode burn-in is in WP-19.

capabilities.capability: Rototracking and a healing tracker that follow a region across frames and paint or patch it.
capabilities.pro_use: Paint fixes and rotoscoping over many frames.

match.note: Little need without live footage; fits the compositor.

capabilities.capability: Stylise effects: toon shading, drop shadow, bevel, border, glow and erode, bloom, grain, halftone and print looks, mosaic, posterise, antialiasing.
capabilities.pro_use: Finishing looks for cel and graphic styles.

match.note: Cel shadows and rims, ground shadows and grain exist. Glow and bloom are in WP-36, halftone and medium looks in WP-15.

capabilities.capability: Transitions: fade, blinds, blocks, page turn, rotary and slide, and blur transitions.
capabilities.pro_use: Scene changes in animatics and finished films.

match.note: Whoosh cuts and crossfaded audio at cut points exist. Cross-dissolves, match cuts and wipes are in WP-15.

capabilities.capability: KeyFramer: moves any element (brush, layer, spare image, paper) along keyed or preset paths, with rotation on three axes, motion blur and pre/post behaviour.
capabilities.pro_use: Animated graphic elements and flying props without redrawing.

match.note: Keyed placement, paths for props and characters, ballistic flights and drops exist. Motion blur is WP-15, and 3D-style rotations of 2D layers WP-36.

capabilities.capability: Multiplane camera: background planes at different depths, each moving at its own speed for parallax.
capabilities.pro_use: Classic depth in pans across layered backgrounds.

match.note: Some sets have built-in parallax depths; true multiplane depth for any layers is in WP-36.

capabilities.capability: Depth-of-field blur set by a focus distance on the multiplane camera.
capabilities.pro_use: Focus pulls between foreground and background.

match.note: Depth of field is in WP-36's multiplane scope.

capabilities.capability: Stage views (perspective, side, front, top) for arranging planes in space.
capabilities.pro_use: Layout artists place planes with confidence.

match.note: A three.js renderer places 3D sets; 2D multiplane layout and its views are in WP-36.

capabilities.capability: A multiplane wizard that builds planes from layers automatically.
capabilities.pro_use: Sets up depth fast from an existing layered background.

match.note: Automatic depth estimates for parallax (Depth Anything) are in WP-43.

capabilities.capability: A particle generator: emitters (shape, rate, life, size, colour), a world (gravity, wind) and particles drawn with any brush, for rain, snow, smoke, fireworks or fountains.
capabilities.pro_use: Natural effects that would take days to draw by hand.

match.note: Seeded particle presets (rain, snow, confetti) exist alongside motion effects and prop gravity; emitters with shape, rate and life are WP-42.

capabilities.capability: Keyboard shortcut configuration for nearly every action.
capabilities.pro_use: Artists tune their hands-on speed.

match.note: Agents call commands by name; Studio's shortcuts are fixed and few.

capabilities.capability: Interface language and resolution scaling.
capabilities.pro_use: Multilingual teams and high-DPI or tablet screens.

match.note: In-house tool with one owner; Studio is a web page that follows the browser's zoom.

capabilities.capability: Pen and tablet settings: eraser-end behaviour, pressure handling, OS tablet APIs.
capabilities.pro_use: Makes the pen feel right on each artist's hardware.

match.note: Pointer pressure works in the Rig Canvas; full tablet support is in WP-18.

capabilities.capability: Save alarm and backup settings.
capabilities.pro_use: Prevents losing work after a crash.

match.note: Every Studio edit is written to the film's files immediately and validated, and git keeps the history.

capabilities.capability: Startup configurations (panel layouts, tools, shortcuts) and a default template.
capabilities.pro_use: Studios give every seat the same setup.

match.note: The machine setup is checked (engine.doctor) and films start from templates. Per-role setups are in WP-21.

capabilities.capability: Timeline and sound preferences (default lengths, audio scrub, playback sync).
capabilities.pro_use: Matches playback behaviour to the work.

match.note: Audio behaviour in Studio is in WP-40.

capabilities.capability: A scripting language that drives almost every tool: layers, drawing, saving, bookmarks.
capabilities.pro_use: Technical directors automate repetitive pipeline tasks.

match.note: Every feature is an @command, available at once in the CLI, the HTTP API, Studio and MCP. Agents are the main users.

capabilities.capability: Scripts as plain text files that run from panel buttons or at startup.
capabilities.pro_use: Pipeline scripts are kept in version control and shared.

match.note: python -m dbe <command> '<json>' runs any command; the tools/ scripts are plain files in git.

capabilities.capability: Passing arguments to scripts and choosing launch modes.
capabilities.pro_use: Scripts are parameterised per shot or per project.

match.note: Every command has a JSON input schema, and results are JSON-safe.

capabilities.capability: Querying project state from scripts (layers, frames, current settings).
capabilities.pro_use: Scripts make decisions from the current scene.

match.note: These return sources, resolved timing and validation results as JSON.

capabilities.capability: Language features: variables, operators, strings, arrays, functions and procedures, parsing.
capabilities.pro_use: Write non-trivial tools inside the program.

match.note: Doodleberry is written in Python and JS directly, so no in-app language is needed.

capabilities.capability: A plug-in SDK (C/C++, now hosted on GitHub) for native extensions.
capabilities.pro_use: Studios add native tools and integrations.

match.note: A new @command appears everywhere at once; vendored upstream code is built and recorded (WP-33).

capabilities.capability: Script dialogs and messages for interacting with the user.
capabilities.pro_use: Tools ask artists for options at run time.

match.note: Commands take arguments and return results; human approvals go through the board and posting gates.

capabilities.capability: A search engine across brushes, panels, shortcuts, clips, layers, library and projects (12.1).
capabilities.pro_use: Finds tools and assets quickly in large configurations.

match.note: Commands are listed with their schemas, and the cast library lists puppets with licence and voice.

capabilities.capability: Loop playback over a selected frame range (12.1).
capabilities.pro_use: Reviews one action repeatedly while fixing it.

match.note: The player scrubs and plays; range loops in review are in WP-19.

capabilities.capability: Official ProRes encoding on every operating system (12.1).
capabilities.pro_use: Broadcast and post-production deliveries.

match.note: ProRes with alpha is in WP-23.

capabilities.capability: Faster handling of projects above 4K (12.1).
capabilities.pro_use: Feature-film and print resolutions.

match.note: Vector art renders at any resolution; 4K masters and EXR passes are in WP-37.

capabilities.capability: A page listing third-party components the documentation uses, with their licence texts.
capabilities.pro_use: Compliance: every bundled component's licence is on record.

match.note: Doodleberry records every component with its licence class and flags restricted classes when a film is posted publicly.
